title: When AI Gives the Answer, Who Does the Learning?
subtitle: AI 給了答案，那學習的是誰？
source: 原創議題文章；研究內容依 Bastani et al.（PNAS, 2025）原文與 Kosmyna et al.（arXiv 預印本, 2025）摘要，2026-10-22 核對

sources.title: Bastani, H. et al. (2025). Generative AI without guardrails can harm learning: Evidence from high school mathematics. PNAS 122(26).
Kosmyna, N. et al. (2025). Your Brain on ChatGPT: Accumulation of Cognitive Debt when Using an AI Assistant for Essay Writing Task. arXiv:2506.08872 (preprint).
Plutarch, On Listening to Lectures (Moralia, Loeb ed., 1927), via LacusCurtius

beginner.title: Help Now, Harder Later?
paras: Many students now use AI chatbots for homework. You type a question, and a few seconds later you get a clear answer. It feels very helpful. But here is a question: when the AI does the work, are you still learning?
現在很多學生用 AI 聊天機器人寫作業。你打一個問題，幾秒後就得到清楚的答案，感覺非常有幫助。但有個問題：當 AI 幫你做完功課，你還在學習嗎？

Researchers tested this in a big high school in Turkey. Nearly 1,000 students did math practice in class. Some students used a normal chatbot, like ChatGPT. Some used a special “AI tutor”. Others used no AI at all. After the practice, everyone took a test without any help. The math topics were ones they had already studied.
研究人員在土耳其一所大型高中測試了這個問題。將近一千名學生在課堂上做數學練習。有些學生用一般的聊天機器人，像 ChatGPT；有些用特別設計的「AI 家教」；其他人完全不用 AI。練習結束後，每個人都在沒有任何協助的情況下參加考試。這些數學主題是他們之前已經學過的。

During practice, the AI groups did much better. Students with the normal chatbot scored 48% higher than students with no AI. But on the test, the normal chatbot group did worse — 17% lower than the students who never used AI. Many of them had simply asked for answers and copied them.
練習時，用 AI 的組別表現好很多。用一般聊天機器人的學生，分數比沒用 AI 的學生高了 48%。但到了考試，一般聊天機器人組反而表現更差——比從沒用過 AI 的學生低了 17%。他們很多人只是要答案，然後照抄。

The AI tutor group was different. Their tutor gave help but was designed to protect learning, and students used it to ask for help and try answers themselves. On the test, they did about as well as the students with no AI. Interestingly, the students who copied answers did not think they had learned less.
AI 家教組就不一樣了。他們的家教會提供協助，但設計上是為了保護學習，學生用它來求助，並自己嘗試作答。考試時，他們的表現和沒用 AI 的學生差不多。有意思的是，那些照抄答案的學生，並不覺得自己學得比較少。

So AI is not good or bad by itself. It depends on how we use it. If AI thinks for us, our brains do less work, and we learn less. If AI helps us think, it can be useful. Try this: write your own answer first, and then ask AI to check it.
所以 AI 本身沒有好壞之分，要看我們怎麼用它。如果 AI 替我們思考，我們的大腦就做得比較少，學到的也比較少。如果 AI 幫助我們思考，它就很有用。試試看：先寫下你自己的答案，再請 AI 幫你檢查。

intermediate.title: When AI Gives the Answer, Who Does the Learning?
paras: Generative AI can now solve a maths problem, summarise a chapter or draft an essay in seconds. For students, the temptation is obvious. But there is a difference between completing a task and learning from it. If a chatbot does the thinking, does the student still build the skill — or only the appearance of one?
生成式 AI 現在可以在幾秒內解出數學題、摘要一章課文，或寫出一篇文章草稿。對學生來說，誘惑顯而易見。但完成一項任務和從中學到東西，是兩回事。如果聊天機器人替學生思考，學生還能培養出能力嗎——還是只培養出能力的假象？

A large experiment published in 2025 offers one answer. Researchers worked with a high school in Turkey, where nearly 1,000 students in about fifty classes took part in four 90-minute maths sessions. Students were randomly given one of three conditions: a standard chatbot based on GPT-4 (“GPT Base”), a version with guardrails designed with teachers’ input (“GPT Tutor”), or no AI. Afterwards, all students took an exam on their own. Each session followed the same pattern: a teacher first reviewed a topic, such as combinatorics, then students practised, and finally they took a test. During practice, every group could also use their notes and textbook.

2025 年發表的一項大型實驗提供了一個答案。研究人員與土耳其一所高中合作，約五十個班、將近一千名學生參加了四次各 90 分鐘的數學課程。學生被隨機分配到三種情況之一：以 GPT-4 為基礎的一般聊天機器人（GPT Base）、依教師意見設計防護機制的版本（GPT Tutor），或完全不用 AI。之後，所有學生都獨自參加考試。每次課程都依照同樣的流程：老師先複習一個主題，例如排列組合，接著學生練習，最後考試。練習時，每一組也都可以使用筆記和課本。

During practice, AI made a big difference: compared with the no-AI group, scores rose by 48% with GPT Base and by 127% with GPT Tutor. The exam told a different story. Students who had used GPT Base scored 17% lower than those who had never had access. An analysis of their chats showed that many had used it as a “crutch”, asking for solutions and copying them.
練習期間，AI 造成了很大的差異：和沒用 AI 的組相比，GPT Base 組分數提高了 48%，GPT Tutor 組提高了 127%。考試卻是另一回事。用過 GPT Base 的學生，分數比從未使用過的學生低了 17%。對話紀錄分析顯示，很多人把它當成「拐杖」，直接要解答然後照抄。

GPT Tutor students, by contrast, used the tool to ask for help and attempt answers independently. Their harmful effect essentially disappeared, though they did not do better than the control group either. Perhaps most worrying, students who copied solutions did not believe they had learned less. The tool made them feel more capable than they were.
相較之下，GPT Tutor 組的學生用這個工具來求助，並自己嘗試作答。他們的負面效果基本上消失了，不過也沒有比對照組表現得更好。最令人擔憂的或許是：照抄解答的學生，並不認為自己學得比較少。這個工具讓他們覺得自己比實際上更有能力。

The lesson is not that students should avoid AI, but that design and habits matter. A tool that hands over answers removes the effort that learning requires. A tool — or a student — that keeps the thinking on the human side can turn AI into a coach rather than a substitute. One practical habit: attempt the problem first, then use AI to check your reasoning, not to replace it.
這個教訓不是學生應該避開 AI，而是設計與習慣很重要。直接交出答案的工具，拿走了學習所需要的努力。而一個讓思考留在人這一邊的工具——或學生——可以把 AI 變成教練，而不是替身。一個實用的習慣是：先自己嘗試解題，再用 AI 檢查你的推理，而不是取代它。

advanced.title: Performance, Learning and the Crutch Problem
paras: Few technologies have entered classrooms as quickly as generative AI. A chatbot can now produce a worked solution, a summary or a polished paragraph faster than most students can read the question. Much of the public debate has focused on cheating. A more fundamental question concerns learning itself: if a tool improves what students produce, does it also improve what they can do once the tool is gone?
很少有技術像生成式 AI 這樣迅速進入教室。聊天機器人現在產出完整解題、摘要或潤飾過的段落的速度，比大多數學生讀完題目還快。公眾辯論多半聚焦在作弊上。一個更根本的問題，關乎學習本身：如果一個工具改善了學生的產出，它是否也改善了學生在沒有這個工具之後的能力？

A preregistered field experiment published in PNAS in 2025 addressed exactly this distinction. Working with a large high school in Turkey during the 2023–2024 school year, researchers ran four 90-minute maths sessions for about fifty classes, comprising nearly 1,000 students. Students were randomly assigned to one of three arms: GPT Base, which mimicked a standard ChatGPT interface; GPT Tutor, built on the same model but with guardrails designed from teacher input; or no AI. Each session followed three stages: a teacher’s review of a previously taught topic, an assisted practice period in which all students also had their notes and textbook, and finally an unassisted exam.

2025 年發表於《美國國家科學院院刊》（PNAS）的一項事先登記的田野實驗，正面處理了這個區別。研究人員在 2023–2024 學年與土耳其一所大型高中合作，為約五十個班、將近一千名學生進行了四次 90 分鐘的數學課程。學生被隨機分配到三組之一：模仿一般 ChatGPT 介面的 GPT Base；以同一模型打造、但依教師意見加入防護機制的 GPT Tutor；或不使用 AI。每次課程分三個階段：老師複習先前教過的主題；有輔助的練習時段，所有學生也都可以使用筆記和課本；最後是無輔助的考試。

The results separate performance from learning with unusual clarity. On practice problems, GPT Base raised scores by 48% relative to the control group, and GPT Tutor by 127%. On the unassisted exam, however, GPT Base students scored 17% lower than students who had never had access. The guardrails in GPT Tutor essentially eliminated this harm, although they produced no measurable gain. Interaction logs explained the pattern: GPT Base was frequently used as a “crutch” to request and copy solutions, whereas GPT Tutor prompted more substantive use, such as asking for help or attempting answers independently.

這些結果以少見的清晰度，把「表現」和「學習」區分開來。在練習題上，GPT Base 讓分數比對照組提高了 48%，GPT Tutor 提高了 127%。然而在無輔助的考試中，GPT Base 組的學生比從未使用過的學生低了 17%。GPT Tutor 的防護機制基本上消除了這種傷害，雖然沒有帶來可測量的進步。互動紀錄解釋了這個模式：GPT Base 經常被當作「拐杖」，用來索取並照抄解答；GPT Tutor 則促成更實質的使用，例如求助或自己嘗試作答。

Perhaps the most troubling finding concerns self-perception. Students who had leaned on GPT Base did not perceive that they had learned less or performed worse, and GPT Tutor students believed they had done significantly better than they actually had. This mismatch echoes a familiar problem in learning research: fluent, effortless experiences feel like progress even when little is retained. A preliminary MIT study, released as a preprint and involving only 54 participants, points in a similar direction: people who wrote essays with an AI assistant showed the weakest brain connectivity and struggled to quote their own work.

最令人不安的發現，或許與自我認知有關。依賴 GPT Base 的學生，並不覺得自己學得較少或表現較差；GPT Tutor 組的學生則認為自己表現得比實際上好得多。這種落差呼應了學習研究中一個常見的問題：流暢、不費力的經驗，即使幾乎沒留下什麼，也會讓人感覺在進步。一項麻省理工學院的初步研究（以預印本發表，只有 54 名參與者）也指向類似方向：用 AI 助手寫作文的人，大腦連結最弱，而且難以準確引用自己寫的內容。

None of this implies that AI should be banned from schools. The same model produced very different outcomes depending on how it was designed and used. The deeper principle is that learning requires the learner to do the cognitive work: to retrieve, to struggle, to make and correct mistakes. Tools that remove that effort optimise for the wrong outcome. The challenge for teachers and students alike is to use AI in ways that keep the thinking — and the responsibility for it — firmly on the human side.
這一切並不代表應該在學校禁用 AI。同一個模型，因為設計與使用方式不同，產生了截然不同的結果。更深層的原則是：學習需要學習者自己做認知工作——提取、掙扎、犯錯再修正。拿走這些努力的工具，是在為錯誤的目標做最佳化。對老師和學生而言，挑戰都在於：以能讓思考——以及思考的責任——牢牢留在人這一邊的方式使用 AI。

quote.text: For the mind does not require filling like a bottle, but rather, like wood, it only requires kindling to create in it an impulse to think independently and an ardent desire for the truth.
quote.author: Plutarch
quote.work: On Listening to Lectures (Moralia), Loeb translation by F. C. Babbitt, 1927

beginner.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How to build an AI tutor for a high school.
Why students in Turkey are better at math than others.
How the way students use AI affects how much they learn.
Why AI chatbots always give wrong math answers.
beginner.evidence: It depends on how we use it.
beginner.why: 全文：同樣是 AI，拿來抄答案會學得更少，拿來輔助思考則不會。
traps: 以偏概全：AI 家教只是實驗中的一組。
捏造：文中沒有跨國比較數學能力。
正反顛倒：AI 組練習時分數反而更高。

beginner.q: What does “Their tutor” in the fourth paragraph refer to?
options: The special AI tutor used by one group.
The math teacher at the high school.
The normal chatbot like ChatGPT.
The test that everyone took alone.
beginner.evidence: The AI tutor group was different.
beginner.why: 前一句說的是 AI 家教組，Their tutor 就是他們用的 AI 家教。
traps: 捏造：文中沒有提到老師當家教。
張冠李戴：一般聊天機器人是另一組用的。
原文字眼、錯誤關係：測驗是最後的評量，不是家教。

beginner.q: Which of the following is true according to the passage?
options: The students who copied answers knew they had learned less.
The normal chatbot group did 48% better on the final test.
The AI tutor group did much better on the test than everyone.
The normal chatbot group did 17% worse on the test than the no-AI group.
beginner.evidence: the normal chatbot group did worse — 17% lower than the students who never used AI
beginner.why: 第三段：考試時一般聊天機器人組比沒用 AI 的低 17%。
traps: 正反顛倒：他們並不覺得自己學得比較少。
時序錯置：48% 是練習時的表現，不是考試。
過度推論：AI 家教組只是和沒用 AI 的差不多。

beginner.q: What does the writer suggest students should do?
options: Copy the AI’s answers to finish homework faster.
Write their own answer first and then ask AI to check it.
Stop using every kind of AI tool at school.
Ask the AI to take the test for them.
beginner.evidence: write your own answer first, and then ask AI to check it
traps: 正反顛倒：抄答案正是讓人學得少的用法。
過度推論：作者說 AI 本身沒有好壞，不是要全部停用。
捏造：考試時本來就不能用任何幫助。

intermediate.q: Which of the following best states the main idea of the passage?
options: GPT Tutor helped students do much better than the control group.
Students who use AI always learn more than those who do not.
Teachers in Turkey have banned AI from maths classes.
AI can boost practice scores but hurt learning unless it is designed and used well.
intermediate.evidence: The lesson is not that students should avoid AI, but that design and habits matter.
intermediate.why: 最後一段點出主旨：設計和使用習慣決定 AI 是幫手還是替身。
traps: 正反顛倒：GPT Tutor 只是和對照組差不多。
正反顛倒：GPT Base 組考試反而較差。
捏造：學校是和研究者合作做實驗。

intermediate.q: What does the word “crutch” in the third paragraph suggest about how students used GPT Base?
options: They used it to check their own reasoning.
They relied on it to do the work for them.
They used it to review topics with the teacher.
They avoided it because it was too difficult.
intermediate.evidence: many had used it as a “crutch”, asking for solutions and copying them
intermediate.why: 拐杖的比喻：依賴它代替自己走路，也就是直接要答案來抄。
traps: 張冠李戴：這是作者建議的好習慣。
原文字眼、錯誤關係：老師複習是每節課的第一步。
正反顛倒：他們是過度使用，不是不用。

intermediate.q: Which of the following is true according to the passage?
options: Students could not use notes or textbooks during practice.
On the exam, GPT Tutor students scored 17% lower than others.
During practice, scores rose by 127% with GPT Tutor.
The students took two 90-minute maths sessions in total.
intermediate.evidence: scores rose by 48% with GPT Base and by 127% with GPT Tutor
traps: 正反顛倒：原文 every group could also use their notes and textbook。
張冠李戴：考試低 17% 的是 GPT Base 組。
數字錯位：一共四次、每次 90 分鐘。

intermediate.q: Why does the author call one finding “most worrying”?
options: Students who copied answers felt more capable than they really were.
Students who used GPT Tutor refused to take the exam.
Teachers could not tell which students had used AI.
The chatbot gave many students wrong maths answers.
intermediate.evidence: The tool made them feel more capable than they were.
intermediate.why: 第四段：抄答案的學生不覺得自己學得少，工具讓他們高估了自己。
traps: 捏造：所有學生都參加了考試。
捏造：文中沒討論老師能否分辨。
捏造：問題在學生抄答案，不是答案錯。

advanced.q: What is the main purpose of the passage?
options: To show that AI can improve performance without improving learning.
To argue that AI should be banned from every school.
To describe how a chatbot is built from teacher input.
To prove that AI tools always make students cheat.
advanced.evidence: The results separate performance from learning with unusual clarity.
advanced.why: 第三段：研究清楚區分了「表現」和「學習」。
traps: 正反顛倒：原文 None of this implies that AI should be banned。
以偏概全：GPT Tutor 的設計只是實驗的一部分。
以偏概全：作者說作弊只是表面的討論，重點在學習。

advanced.q: Which of the following is closest in meaning to “guardrails” as used in the second paragraph?
options: Teachers who watch students during exams.
Fences that protect students in the school.
Built-in limits that steer how a tool is used.
Rules that ban AI from the classroom.
advanced.evidence: GPT Tutor, built on the same model but with guardrails designed from teacher input
advanced.why: 同一個模型加上依教師意見設計的限制，引導學生正確使用。
traps: 捏造：監考不是這個詞的意思。
字面誤讀：guardrail 原指護欄，這裡是比喻。
正反顛倒：GPT Tutor 正是在教室裡使用的 AI。

advanced.q: Which of the following is true according to the passage?
options: GPT Base students realised that they had learned less.
GPT Tutor students believed they had done better than they actually had.
GPT Tutor produced a large gain on the unassisted exam.
The MIT study involved about 1,000 participants.
advanced.evidence: GPT Tutor students believed they had done significantly better than they actually had
traps: 正反顛倒：他們並不覺得自己學得少。
正反顛倒：原文 they produced no measurable gain。
數字錯位：MIT 研究只有 54 人，1,000 人是土耳其的實驗。

advanced.q: According to the last paragraph, why do tools that remove effort “optimise for the wrong outcome”?
options: AI models are too expensive for schools.
Students prefer tools that are difficult to use.
Teachers cannot grade work done with AI.
Learning depends on the learner doing the cognitive work.
advanced.evidence: learning requires the learner to do the cognitive work
advanced.why: 最後一段：學習需要學習者自己提取、掙扎、犯錯再修正。
traps: 捏造：文中沒談成本。
捏造：文中沒提學生的偏好。
捏造：文中沒談評分。

reflections: Think of the last time you used AI for schoolwork. Was it helping you think, or thinking instead of you?
Design one rule that would make AI-assisted homework more meaningful. How would a teacher check that it works?

A chatbot can now produce a worked solution, a summary or a polished paragraph faster than most students can read the question. Much of the public debate has focused on cheating. A more basic question, however, concerns learning itself: if a tool improves what students produce, does it also improve what they can do once the tool is gone?
很少有科技像生成式 AI 這樣快速進入教室。聊天機器人產出解題過程、摘要或一段漂亮文字的速度，比多數學生讀完題目還快。大眾的討論多半聚焦在作弊。然而更根本的問題是學習本身：如果一個工具讓學生的作品變好，等工具拿走以後，學生的能力也變好了嗎？

A large experiment published in 2025 addressed exactly this question. Working with a high school in Turkey, researchers ran four 90-minute maths sessions for about fifty classes, involving nearly 1,000 students. Students were randomly given one of three conditions: GPT Base, which copied a standard ChatGPT interface; GPT Tutor, built on the same model but with guardrails (limits designed with teachers’ input); or no AI. Each session followed three stages — a teacher’s review of a topic, a practice period in which every group could also use notes and textbooks, and finally an exam taken without any help.

2025 年發表的一項大型實驗，正好回答了這個問題。研究者和土耳其一所高中合作，為大約五十個班、將近一千名學生開了四次 90 分鐘的數學課。學生被隨機分到三種條件之一：GPT Base，仿照一般的 ChatGPT 介面；GPT Tutor，用同一個模型，但加上依教師意見設計的限制；或完全不用 AI。每次課程分三個階段——老師複習一個主題、一段每組都能使用筆記和課本的練習時間，最後是一場不能使用任何協助的考試。

The results separate performance from learning with unusual clarity. On practice problems, GPT Base raised scores by 48 percent compared with the no-AI group, and GPT Tutor by 127 percent. Yet on the exam, GPT Base students scored 17 percent lower than students who had never had access. Records of the chats explained why: many had used GPT Base as a “crutch”, simply asking for solutions and copying them. GPT Tutor students, by contrast, asked for help and tried answers on their own, and the harm essentially disappeared, though they did not do better than the control group either.

結果罕見地清楚區分了「表現」和「學習」。練習題上，GPT Base 讓分數比不用 AI 的組高了 48%，GPT Tutor 更高出 127%。但到了考試，GPT Base 組的分數比從沒用過 AI 的學生低了 17%。對話紀錄說明了原因：很多人把 GPT Base 當「拐杖」，直接要答案來抄。相反地，GPT Tutor 組的學生是請求協助、自己嘗試作答，傷害基本上消失了，雖然他們也沒有考得比對照組好。

Perhaps the most troubling finding concerns how students saw themselves. Those who had leaned on GPT Base did not believe they had learned less, and GPT Tutor students thought they had done much better than they actually had. So easily does effortless work feel like progress that students may not notice when little is being learned. A small early study at MIT, involving only 54 people, points in a similar direction: those who wrote essays with an AI assistant struggled to quote their own work.
最令人不安的發現，或許是學生怎麼看自己。依賴 GPT Base 的學生不覺得自己學得比較少，GPT Tutor 組的學生則以為自己考得比實際好很多。毫不費力的作業太容易讓人覺得有進步，以致學生可能察覺不到自己學得很少。麻省理工學院一項只有 54 人參與的小型初步研究也指向類似方向：用 AI 助手寫作文的人，很難引用自己寫過的內容。

None of this means that AI should be banned from schools. It was the same model that produced very different outcomes, depending on how it was designed and used. Learning, after all, requires the learner to do the thinking: to recall, to struggle, and to make and correct mistakes. Tools that remove that effort aim at the wrong goal. The challenge for teachers and students alike is to keep the thinking firmly on the human side.
這一切並不表示學校應該禁用 AI。同一個模型，會因為設計和使用方式不同，帶來截然不同的結果。畢竟，學習需要學習者自己動腦：回想、掙扎、犯錯再修正。把這些努力拿掉的工具，追求的是錯的目標。老師和學生共同的挑戰，是讓思考牢牢留在人的這一邊。

questions.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: Why students prefer textbooks to AI tools.
Why every school in Turkey has banned AI chatbots.
How to build a chatbot that gives correct answers.
How AI can raise practice scores without improving learning.
questions.evidence: The results separate performance from learning with unusual clarity.
questions.why: 全文：AI 讓練習分數變高，卻可能讓真正的學習變差，關鍵在設計和使用。
traps: 捏造：文中沒有比較學生的偏好。
正反顛倒：作者說不應禁用，學校是和研究者合作做實驗。
捏造：問題不在答案對錯。

options: Students used the tool to check their reasoning.
Students relied on the tool instead of thinking.
Students were injured during the maths sessions.
Students avoided the tool because it was difficult.
questions.evidence: simply asking for solutions and copying them
questions.why: 拐杖的比喻：依賴它代替自己走，也就是直接要答案來抄。
traps: 張冠李戴：這比較像 GPT Tutor 組的用法。
字面誤讀：crutch 是比喻，不是真的受傷。
正反顛倒：他們是過度使用。

GPT Tutor students scored 17 percent lower on the exam.

The study included only one class of students.
